---
title: "ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_app_login_counts"
description: "Daily SSO event counts by application."
---

Daily SSO event counts for each CanadaLogin-integrated application.

Each row is one application on one day. It counts what IBM Verify calls the
`sso` event type, raised when someone who is already signed in reaches an
application.

[`events_auth_total_logins`](events_auth_total_logins.qmd) counts a different
event type (`authentication`). Never add the two tables' figures together or
show them side by side.

`Keywords`: SSO events, application usage, sign-ins, logins, applications, unique users, adoption, daily counts

## Provenance

Built from [`application_usage`](../ibm_verify_events_raw/application_usage.qmd)
by `compute_app_login_counts()` in the [daily metrics
job](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/ibm_verify_events_streaming/glue_src/ibm_verify_events_metrics_daily.py).

* **Updated**: Daily, at 04:00 ET, for the previous ET day
* **Retention**: While CanadaLogin exists
* **Steward**: EDCP Data and Research Team
* **Contact**: [Yinlin Zhang](mailto:yinlin.zhang@cds-snc.ca)
* **Location**: `s3://<transformed-bucket>/ibm_verify_metrics/events_app_login_counts/`

## Fields

One row per `application_id` per day.

| Field Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| application_id | string | IBM Verify's numeric ID for the application |
| application_name | string | The latest name seen for the application that day (for example, "IRIS - PRC - Prod"). Join to [`rp.alias`](../rp/alias.qmd) on this |
| from_date | string | The reporting day in ET, for example "2026-09-15". Cast before comparing to a date |
| to_date | string | Same as `from_date` |
| total_logins | bigint | SSO events for the application that day. Counts events, not people |
| unique_users | bigint | Distinct users with an SSO event for the application that day, successful or not |
| failed_logins | bigint | Failed SSO events that day |
| successful_logins | bigint | Successful SSO events that day |
| mtd_unique_users | bigint | Distinct users of the application month-to-date. Resets on the 1st |
| ytd_unique_users | bigint | Distinct users of the application year-to-date. Resets on January 1 |
| fetched_at | string | When the job wrote the row, in ISO 8601 UTC |
| date | string | Partition key. Same as `from_date` |

## Notes

`total_logins`, `unique_users`, `failed_logins`, and `successful_logins` are
daily values. The `mtd_` and `ytd_` columns are cumulative: take the latest
value in the window, never sum them.

**One row per ID.** On 2026-10-19 every application name had exactly one ID. If
a name ever gets two, summing `unique_users` across them double-counts people who
used both.

**Join to relying parties after, not before, aggregating.** Several application
names can map to one service. See [Joining through the lookup](../rp.qmd#joining-through-the-lookup).

**Failed events rarely have a user.** In September 2026, 17,650 of 17,674 failed
SSO events had the user ID `"UNKNOWN"`, which counts as one user that day.

**Not inflated by second factors.** Reaching an application uses the session the
person already holds, so one handoff is one SSO event. `total_logins` still
counts events, because one person can reach an application many times.
